_comment: Seats for brood-conclave. One seat per family. `lines` are the family's product lines, best first: the resolver takes the newest version of the first line the OpenRouter catalog carries (so Opus 6 replaces Opus 5.5 inside the claude-opus line without an edit). A line it has never seen (say a new Gemini flagship) is adopted automatically when it was released after the current pick and is priced at least `adopt_ratio` of it; `lower_lines` never trigger that. `variants` are name tokens that mark a variant of a line rather than a line (gpt-6-astra-pro), and such ids are never picked. `pin` (an OpenRouter-style id) overrides everything. `routes` are harnesses tried in order when Lor-only mode is disabled (`--no-lor`); every route runs with web search on, and `conclave doctor` proves it. `opencode` goes through OpenRouter; `opencode-direct` uses the vendor's own API key (no OpenRouter, so no OpenRouter ZDR refusal) with Exa search. No script names a model: ids come from the catalogs. `lor` runs the seat as a Lor subagent on the Lor router with full sandbox tools and `lor web search`/`lor web fetch`, only inside a Lor session (LOR_SESSION_ID set); top-level `lor` defaults to true so all seats run exclusively through Lor subagents unless `--no-lor`, `CONCLAVE_LOR=0`, or `"lor": false` is set. `lor_ids` maps a catalog id to the Lor router id where the two differ beyond dots becoming dashes.
